The U.S. Marine Corps Ground Renewable Expeditionary Energy Network Systems can power a battalion-size combat operations center, and the Solar Portable Alternative Communication Energy System charges radio batteries (Cusack 2023). The U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center’s first operational hydrogen- powered nanogrid in a remote area of the White Sands Missile Range is demonstrating the potential of hydrogen energy systems to provide localized, sustainable power in military settings, particularly in remote areas (Kilgore 2025). DOW’s Environmental Security Technology Certification Program (ESTCP) tests and validates innovative technologies at military sites. The program addresses transition challenges through detailed, well-documented demonstrations that supply critical information to all DOW stakeholders, facilitating the transition and adoption of new technologies (SERDP and ESTCP 2023).
